status_note: First-authored draft. Evidence base is fully sourced from whitepaper 02_concurrent_training.md — 32 primary citations. Weekly template + block structure are the initial engineering proposal; will refine after beta feedback.

goals.primary: Add aerobic capacity without losing strength
goals.secondary: Preserve explosive strength within the documented Schumann 2022 SMD −0.28 bound
explicit_non_goals: Hitting new 1RM PRs during this block (PR chasing violates RPE ≤ 7 ceiling)

principles.rule: Concurrent training has a cost. We bound and cite it, we don't pretend it's zero.
principles.detail: Schumann 2022 meta (43 studies): maximal strength SMD −0.06 (n.s.), hypertrophy SMD −0.01 (n.s.), explosive strength SMD −0.28 (p=0.007). We accept the max/hypertrophy bounds; we structure to protect explosive strength.

principles.rule: Minimum 6 hours between endurance and strength sessions on same day.
principles.detail: Robineau 2016 dose-response tested 0h / 6h / 24h and found 0h significantly reduced bench + half-squat gains vs the other two. 24h was best. Our 6h floor is a practical engineering read of that curve, not a paper-validated threshold — see engineering_choices_flagged.

principles.rule: When same-day pairing is unavoidable, lift first.
principles.detail: Eddens 2018: resistance-before-endurance produced +6.91% greater lower-body dynamic strength gain vs endurance-first (p=0.006).

principles.rule: Cycling / rowing / ski-erg preferred over running for the strength athlete.
principles.detail: Wilson 2012 (r = −0.26 to −0.35 frequency, −0.29 to −0.75 duration): running produces more interference than cycling; cycling near-zero. Doma 2019: bidirectional damage — running-induced damage impairs subsequent squat/deadlift force 24-48h.

principles.rule: RPE ≤ 7 on all strength sessions during the block.
principles.detail: Prevents chasing the explosive-strength cost (Schumann 2022 SMD −0.28). Maintenance dose, not build.

principles.rule: Endurance volume mediates interference. Intensity does not (much).
principles.detail: Fyfe 2016: HIT+RT and MICT+RT produced same strength decrement (~0.9% difference). Cap total endurance minutes; don't fear intensity per session.
Morton 2018 meta: hypertrophy response plateaus at 1.62 g/kg/day. Below this floor, concurrent losses are amplified. ISSN position stand (Jäger 2017): 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day.

plan_tiers.label: Foundation
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: submax HR down 5-10 bpm at fixed pace, back squat / bench / deadlift maintained within 2.5 kg of pre-block TM.

plan_tiers.label: Progression
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: Submax HR down 8-15 bpm, strength held or +2.5 kg on any lift (only via green cycle-end).

plan_tiers.label: Push
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: VO2max +2-4%; strength floor held. Above this bar, concurrent gains become stochastic per HERITAGE non-response data.

program_goal.display_name: Submax HR reduction at fixed pace

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Honest answer wins. If your ceiling is 2, we'll tell you upfront whether this program can deliver on its claim at that dose.

questions.label: Do you have a current back-squat 5RM you'd rather not lose?
Do you have high blood pressure that isn't under control? (Over 160/100 at rest, or diagnosed but not on medication — uncontrolled hypertension.)
Ever fainted or had unexplained cardiac symptoms during exertion?
I consent to storing training log and symptom scores.

consent.label: I understand this is training programming, not medical advice.

safety_gates.block_body: Unmanaged hypertension makes high-intensity interval work unsafe. Get BP under management before starting concurrent programming.
History of exertional syncope requires medical clearance before any interval-based program.
Running-based intervals will amplify a flaring tendon. Consider deferring, or the strength-only variant while it settles.

phases.name: Intro · Weeks 1–2
phases.goal: Anchor the strength floor. Introduce Z2 volume. No high-intensity yet.
phases.rationale: The molecular-interference window (Baar 2014: AMPK stays elevated ~3h post-endurance; mTORC1 sensitised 18-24h post-lifting) matters most when intensity is introduced. Weeks 1-2 give the athlete a settled aerobic baseline before we add stress.

phases.name: Intervals · Weeks 3–6
phases.goal: Add Norwegian 4×4 once/week. Hold strength at RPE ≤ 7. Week 4 is the deload.
phases.rationale: Helgerud 2007 dose (4×4 × 3/wk × 8 wk → +7.2% VO2max) is fully compatible with maintenance strength IF the 6h separation rule holds (Robineau 2016).

phases.name: Retest · Weeks 7–8
phases.goal: Retest submax HR at pace-5. Confirm strength held.
phases.rationale: Pre/post submax HR at fixed pace is a threshold-shift proxy (Joyner & Coyle 2008 — track threshold, not VO2max).

blocks.name: Strength · Heavy
blocks.note: RPE 6-7 top set. No PRs. 3 warm-ups + top set + FSL 5×5 @ 65%.

blocks.name: Strength · Moderate
blocks.note: Front squat + press pattern. Volume day, RPE 6.

blocks.name: Zone 2 · Bike
blocks.note: HR at ~70-75% max. Bike preferred over run (Wilson 2012 modality bias).

blocks.name: Zone 2 · Row / Ski
blocks.note: Sustainable pace. Add to Z2 bike volume, don't replace.

blocks.name: Norwegian 4×4 · Row / Ski
blocks.note: 4×4 min @ 90-95% max HR, 3 min active recovery. ≥6h from any lift (Robineau 2016).

blocks.name: Retest · Submax HR
blocks.note: 5 min at fixed pace (e.g. row 2:00/500m), record steady-state HR. Compare to pre-block baseline.

blocks.name: Retest · 5RM confirm
blocks.note: Confirm back-squat + block-pull 5RM held vs pre-block.

blocks.name: Deload · Week 4
blocks.note: 40-50% TM × 5 for all lifts. Volume down 50%. Symptom check.

training_maxes.note: Lifts CSM users actually train in the strength blocks. Values are examples — replaced by the user's own numbers on Progress.

weekly_template.note: Correlated tier: all three tiers use the same weekly layout, scaled by intensity. Foundation drops one Z2 session; Push adds one.
principles: Lift Mon + Wed. Cardio Sun / Tue / Thu / Fri.
Never lift + hard intervals on the same day.
6h min between any two sessions same day.

progression_rules.note: See adapt.ts + suggest.ts. RPE ≤ 7 ceiling holds throughout. Cycle-end evaluation not run (this is a maintenance block, not a 5/3/1 arc).

states.trigger: submax HR ↓ ≥ 3 bpm at pace-5, no strength loss
strength holding but submax HR flat
strength loss > 2.5 kg on any lift OR ≥ 3 amber symptom days in a week
states.action: drop 4×4 for a week; resume next week at 3×4

immediate_actions.action: Establish baseline submax HR at pace-5 in week 1
Confirm current back-squat + block-pull 5RM before starting

physiological_targets.confidence: realistic for Progression tier; stretch for Push

push.confidence: stretch — HERITAGE non-response distribution begins to dominate at this dose

session_rationale.why_lift_twice_weekly: Murach & Bagley 2016 + Schumann 2022 — 2×/wk is sufficient for maintenance in trained lifters. Adding a third session accelerates hypertrophy but also raises the interference cost.
session_rationale.why_norwegian_4x4: Helgerud 2007 4×4 protocol delivered +7.2% VO2max at 3×/wk × 8wk in soccer players. We prescribe 1×/wk to keep the interference cost within Schumann 2022 SMD −0.28 bounds while still driving central adaptations.
session_rationale.why_z2_dominates: Seiler 2010 polarised model — ~80% volume at low intensity, ~10-20% at high. This program follows the shape: 3-4 Z2 sessions to 1 hard session.
session_rationale.why_row_not_run: Wilson 2012 modality interference (running > cycling > rowing). Doma 2019 bidirectional damage. For the strength athlete, rowing / cycling preserve the pull the day after.

concurrent_strength_prescription.reason: Schumann 2022 SMD −0.28 for explosive strength (p=0.007). RPE 7 keeps the athlete out of the neural-fatigue zone that drives the explosive-strength cost.
concurrent_strength_prescription.reason_separation: Robineau 2016 dose-response — 0h significantly reduced gains; 6h preserved them; 24h optimized VO2max.
concurrent_strength_prescription.lift_first_rule: Eddens 2018 — +6.91% lower-body dynamic strength when resistance precedes endurance same day.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Minimum 6h separation between endurance and strength on same day
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: Robineau 2016 tested 0h / 6h / 24h — a 3-point dose-response, not a validated 6h bright-line. The rule stays defensible as an engineering read of that curve, but the paper does not establish 6h as *the* threshold. 24h would be optimal; 6h is our practical minimum.
Concurrent context; full Helgerud dose has never been tested against maintenance strength. Engineering choice biased to strength preservation.
Matches published concurrent RCTs (Wilson 2012 meta window 6-24 wk); minimum for detectable submax HR change per Ross 2015.
Coaching-consensus buffer against neural fatigue overshoot. No RCT specifies the exact ceiling.
Bertolotti-friendly reference from the founder's clinical context. Substitutable per athlete.

contraindications: Unmanaged hypertension (BP > 160/100 at rest) — see clinician before Norwegian 4×4 sessions.
History of exertional syncope or unexplained cardiac symptoms — full clearance first.
First-trimester pregnancy — HR zones are unreliable; work with a specialist.
Flaring lower-limb tendinopathy (Achilles, patellar) — no running variant of intervals.
Post-COVID convalescence with elevated resting HR — defer intervals until baseline HR normalises.
adaptive_engine_hooks: day_adjustment on notes-signal 'legs feel dead / low fuel' → load ×0.95 on next strength session
amber week detection (≥3 amber days) → drop 4×4 next week
no cycle-end TM proposal (maintenance block; TMs held by design)

onboarding_steps.title: The 0-10 scale
onboarding_steps.body_md: You'll rate readiness-to-train and life stress most mornings — not medical, just how you feel today. Here's how the numbers read:

onboarding_steps.title: Life load, today
onboarding_steps.body_md: How heavy is the day around your training right now? Sleep, work, stress, travel. The engine reads this and proposes lighter loads when it's genuinely high.

onboarding_steps.title: What this program does NOT do
onboarding_steps.body_md: Concurrent Strength Maintenance holds your squat / press / deadlift while an aerobic block runs. There are no PR days here. Trying to add PRs against a hard aerobic week is where the interference cost shows up.
